memos.scout:
The case for buying PCAT now is thinner than the headline numbers suggest, but it exists.

Demand is broad and recent. In the last 15 minutes there were 2,167 buyers against 1,609 sellers, with $267k volume, and the coin is up 171% over 30 minutes. Concentration is low: the top 3 curve buyers hold 7% of flow and the top 5 post-graduation buyers 13.5%, which argues against a single wallet controlling exit. Post-graduation buyers (545) outnumber the launch-bot cohort, and the coin has only pulled back 8.6% from its 30-minute high, so it has not broken.

The case against is stronger. Net flow over the last 15 minutes was just +61 SOL on 1,150 SOL of buying, meaning sellers are absorbing almost everything, and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes was 0.88. A 35% bundle share and a launch bot signal coordinated early activity. Pool depth of 186 SOL is shallow for a $220k market cap, so a $20 ticket will face meaningful slippage against a 1.4-5.1% round trip. Age of 31 minutes sits inside the window where random buys have historically lost.

Verdict: a modest, fragile case. Demand is real in count, but sell pressure is keeping pace with it. I would pass unless the desk sees evi
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a late distribution after a parabolic run. PCAT is up 171% over 30 minutes and 56% in the last 15, yet net flow over that window is only +61 SOL on 1,150 SOL of buys against 1,090 SOL of sells, with 1,609 sellers versus 2,167 buyers. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes is 0.88, so early holders have been feeding out steadily. The bundle share of 35% and a launch bot present suggest coordinated early wallets that may still be unwinding. Only 186 SOL of pool depth against roughly $220K market cap means a $20 round trip eats 1.4-5.1% before any move, and the 8.6% drawdown from the high shows the top is already being tested. A coin this extended, with this much two-sided churn and thin liquidity, is more likely to give back a dip than hold the gain.
